title: Delta Federation
rules: Six settlements have farming, building, freight and sluice tools. Any adjacent residents can exchange tools or pass real grain/timber units.
Fields grow on hydraulic phases when their river node has enough water and is not flooded. Grain can be carried by road or loaded onto a one-unit barge.
Every fourth tick is a hydraulic phase. Opening a gate releases at most three units into a visible three-position downstream delay queue.
An embankment raises its field flood tolerance, but high protected water can release an extra unit downstream. Extreme floods damage levees and bridges.
Barges advance one river cell on hydraulic phases only with an open source sluice, enough water at both endpoints and sediment below four.
Builders spend timber on bridges and levees. Operators dredge, close gates or breach a levee; every choice can change other settlements' future water or routes.
Direct granary and rainfall-code knowledge belongs to the home settlement. Adjacent speech creates expiring reports; public trade and rain remain observable.
Storage rewards use signed stock changes; withdrawing grain reverses the deposit potential. Separate rewards mark actual meals, first bridges and navigable routes.
The delta persists through H=512. Hunger, floods and damaged infrastructure are local costs; they do not declare global success or end the world early.
